findings.title: skipToken still grants Grafana Duplicate on non-Grafana rules
findings.body: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is called with skipToken (converted to undefined) whenever the menu has no Grafana Prometheus rule, including every datasource-managed rule. useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(undefined) returns loading:false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported, and Duplicate is then [true, user has Grafana AlertingRuleCreate] via toAbility(getRulesPermissions('grafana').create). AlertRuleMenu ORs that tuple with the ruler ability (canDuplicate), so an editor who may create Grafana-managed rules but may not write external rules still sees Duplicate and the clone flow is started with the cloud rule identifier. skipToken is meant to skip the check, but it does not return [false, false]. View and Explore are the same shape (supported plus a global permission even when the rule is missing) and will leak if callers OR them the same way. Existing RBAC tests mock these hooks, so they never execute this path.

findings.title: Delete stays hidden in the list view without a ruler rule
findings.body: The new list passes only a Prometheus rule into RuleActionsButtons, and AlertRuleMenu now treats the Grafana prom-rule delete ability as enough for canDelete. The Delete item is still rendered only when rulerRule is truthy (canDelete && rulerRule) and the click passes that ruler rule into handleDelete. The list no longer loads ruler rules, so rulerRule is undefined and Delete never appears, even for users with folder delete permission. RuleActionsButtons already ignores the ruler argument and calls showDeleteModal with the uid identifier built from the prom rule, so the gate is leftover and removes an action that would otherwise work.

findings.title: Pause is unreachable once ruler rules are dropped from the list
findings.body: canPause is now true for an editable Grafana alerting rule based on useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, but the Pause item is still rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) is true, and it passes that ruler rule into MenuItemPauseRule. GrafanaRuleListItem never supplies a ruler rule, so Pause cannot appear in the list the PR is migrating. Dropping the rulerRule check is not sufficient: MenuItemPauseRule still requires a RulerGrafanaRuleDTO. The prom rule already has uid and isPaused, but nothing maps those into the pause action, and onPauseChange is not wired from RuleActionsButtons either.

findings.title: Silence menu item does nothing without a ruler rule
findings.body: The list menu shows Silence notifications because useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities allows it for Grafana alerting rules, and handleSilence only sets showSilenceDrawer. The drawer is mounted only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true, where rule is the optional ruler-rule prop. GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule, so that condition is false and the click is a no-op. SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer still requires a RulerGrafanaRuleDTO; the list needs a fetch-on-demand or a drawer that can create the silence from the prom rule uid and labels. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test only asserts the menu item is present and never clicks it.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to set isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) (true when the group has source_tenants) and treat those rules as immutable. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated to false and drops the isFederatedRuleGroup import. useAlertRuleAbility still goes through this for every CombinedRule, not only the new list. Update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent delete therefore become supported for federated Mimir/GEM groups whenever the user otherwise has permission. Editing those rules through the normal form rewrites the ruler group and can strip source_tenants, breaking cross-tenant evaluation.

findings.title: Recording rules lose export and pause in prom-rule abilities
findings.body: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities uses isAlertingRule (Prometheus alerting type only) as the support flag for ModifyExport, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently. The ruler ability path uses isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which is true for both Grafana alerting and recording rules, and the comment here says every GrafanaPromRuleDTO is Grafana-managed by definition. Recording rules in the new list therefore lose Export, and Pause stays unsupported even after the rulerRule menu gate is fixed. Silence correctly depends on alerting type; these other actions should not. Detail views that still use ruler abilities will keep showing Export and Pause for the same recording rule, so the two UIs disagree.

findings.title: Filtered Grafana rows are rendered without React keys
findings.body: FilterViewResults builds a KeyedRuleWithOrigin key specifically to avoid duplicate list keys, and the previous GrafanaRuleLoader was rendered with key={key}. The replacement GrafanaRuleListItem omits that prop, while the datasource and unknown branches in the same map still set key. Grafana rows are therefore unkeyed siblings of keyed rows. As infinite scroll appends pages, React can reuse the wrong row instance (open More menu or silence-drawer state) and will warn about missing keys. getGrafanaRuleKey on line 209 also has a stray closing brace (`rule.uid}}`), so putting key={key} back without fixing that helper still yields malformed keys.

findings.title: Rule view links drop the returnTo back-navigation target
findings.body: The removed list item built the view href with createReturnTo() so the rule detail back link returned to the current list URL, including search filters. The new GrafanaRuleListItem always links to `/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view` with no returnTo query param. Opening a rule from the group list or the filtered list therefore loses that context, and back navigation no longer returns to the same filtered results. Group-loader tests only assert that the href contains the view path, so they do not catch the missing parameter.

findings.title: Menu test asserts the incomplete action set
findings.body: The new More-menu test grants AlertingRuleUpdate and AlertingRuleDelete, defines a Delete menuitem selector, and then asserts the menu contains exactly four items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export). That locks in the missing Delete and Pause actions introduced by dropping ruler rules. It also never clicks Silence, so it does not notice that the drawer does not open. A green run of this file does not cover the list-view action regressions, and RulesTable RBAC tests mock useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities entirely, so they do not execute the skipToken permission logic either.
